hyps.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 is zero, so a conv on 1->3 processes nothing and its gain vanishes.
Edge 2 only transforms node 1, which is empty when edge 0 is none, so the edit is inert.
A direct skip to the output already provides a strong shortcut, so a conv on the parallel 1->3 path adds less.
Replacing none with a conv adds an entire new path into the output, gaining more than replacing an op that already carries signal.
Turning a missing direct input-to-output edge into a conv adds a new path, a bigger gain than refining an existing op.
Replacing none on the final edge restores a route from node 2 to the output, gaining more than swapping one existing op for another.
Replacing none on edge 1 opens a new input path into node 2, giving a larger gain than replacing an op that already carries signal.
A direct skip on edge 3 already gives a trainable shortcut, so a 3x3 conv on the parallel path 1->3 yields a smaller marginal gain.
With a residual shortcut to the output already present, the extra conv on edge 5 saturates and gains less than when edge 3 is none.
Replacing a skip, already a good op, with a conv gains less than replacing none or pooling, and can even hurt.
